title.narrative: Integrated sexual and reproductive health and GBV risk mitigation prevention and response to Sudanese refugees in Libya

description.narrative: Through this CERF submission UNFPA Libya country office seeks to deliver lifesaving emergency services to Sudanese refugees and Third Country Nationals (TCNs) arriving to Al Kufra and extend support to those who recently arrived in Benghazi, Tripoli, Sebha, and Ajdabia. This response is structured based on the CERF lifesaving criteria (provision of MISP and GBV lifesaving engagements), tailored around the needs and implementation arrangements, operational landscape, and complexity in Libya.The project will ensure direct access of 4,400 refugees and host communities to GBV-integrated SRH services. UNFPA is scaling up its response through integration and localization strategies in affected communities intending to maximize access and benefit for affected populations. The GBV and SRH integration model is centered around maximizing access to affected people through one-stop facilities including the establishment of women and girls safe spaces (WGSS) and integration of health services through deployment of community health care workers (CHWs) within these spaces (Al Kufah, Ajdabia, Benghazi, Tripoli, Sebha) to improve referral pathways for GBV survivors. UNFPA will deploy skilled healthcare providers to health facilities in Sebha and Kufrah to provide integrated medical case (Clinical management of rape), psychosocial first aid and MHPSS referral to WHO psychiatric center, in response to the needs of CRSV (conflict related sexual violence) and GBV survivors.Through this CERF project, UNFPA will establish a WGSS in Alkufra, and support the functionality of existing WGSSs in other areas accessible by refugees. The WGSS model is a critical measure for safeguarding and empowering women and girls in crisis and is one of the minimum standards for GBV in emergency programming. WGSSs serve as secure venues for accessing lifesaving integrated GBV/SRH services, they are a communal platform for interaction, information sharing, and leveraging support networks. The support provided through the WGSS helps in mitigating risks and averting additional trauma amidst conflicts. UNFPA reinforces GBV mainstreaming through technical support to other sectors/ task forces, implementing safety audits, and improving the capacity of frontline responders and community members on GBV risk mitigation and safe and ethical GBV disclosures.UNFPA will implement components of the Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) for SRH in emergencies through the deployment of medical teams in AL Kufra and Sebha for the provision of EMONC, prevention of unintended pregnancies, management of sexually transmitted illnesses, and post-abortion care. UNFPA will support the updating of the GBV referral pathways and improve the availability of health response to GBV and MPHSS for survivors of GBV through deployment and training of frontline healthcare providers on CMR & intimate partner violence (IPV), support referral, and access to treatment.UNFPA has an established LTA for immediate placement of the dignity kits procurement which is on standby for immediate production as soon as this CERF project is approved. Localization is considered a key strategy for UNFPA for sustainability. In addition, UNFPA will support existing healthcare delivery points, and the deployed mobile teams will work with the existing care providers through on-the-job training and hands-on job support. UNFPA's partner has a roster of service providers on standby for deployment.Utilizing the latest assessment results, ground preparation by UNFPA with local stakeholders already started, centered around ensuring access, while services will be scaled up in the relevant facilities. UNFPA will deploy community health workers to ensure focused engagement with the affected people in targeted areas and support referrals for provision of necessary care, distribution of dignity kits, and GBV response engagement.
